hints: Focus on what hot concentrated sulfuric acid does to an alcohol, think elimination rather than substitution or oxidation.
Notice menthol is a secondary alcohol on a ring, so losing the $\text{OH}$ plus a hydrogen from a neighbouring carbon will give a $\text{C=C}$ in the ring.
Compare the two possible ring alkenes for substitution around the double bond and pick the more stable, more substituted Zaitsev product.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the reaction type**

Great spot, this is a classic test of functional groups. Hot concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ with an alcohol means acid-catalysed dehydration.

$$\text{R-CH(OH)-CH} \xrightarrow[\text{heat}]{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{R-C=C} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find where the double bond can form**

Menthol is $\text{2-isopropyl-5-methylcyclohexan-1-ol}$, a secondary alcohol. The $\text{OH}$ carbon has two different neighbours: one is the carbon bearing the isopropyl group ($\text{CH}$), the other is a $\text{CH}_2$ in the ring.

Removing $\text{H}$ from either neighbour gives a cyclohexene, so the carbon skeleton with methyl and isopropyl groups stays intact.

**Apply Zaitsev's rule to choose the major alkene**

Elimination favours the more substituted, more stable $\text{C=C}$. Loss of $\text{H}$ from the isopropyl-bearing carbon gives a trisubstituted double bond between C1 and C2, with three alkyl groups attached.

Loss of $\text{H}$ from the $\text{CH}_2$ side gives only a disubstituted double bond. The trisubstituted isomer is the major product T.

options.A: This shows an exocyclic $\text{C=C(CH}_3)_2$ outside the ring. To form this you would need to lose $\text{OH}$ from the ring and $\text{H}$ from a methyl of the isopropyl group, but those carbons are not directly adjacent, so normal E1/E2 dehydration cannot give this directly.
options.B: This shows a ketone $\text{C=O}$ in place of the $\text{CH(OH)}$. That is an oxidation product, formed with reagents like acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$, not with hot concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ which acts as a dehydrating agent here.
options.C: This is a ring alkene, so the reaction type is right, but the double bond is in the less substituted position away from the isopropyl group. It comes from removing $\text{H}$ from the $\text{CH}_2$ side and is the minor, less stable Hofmann-type product, not the major product T.
options.D: This is the ring alkene with the $\text{C=C}$ between the original $\text{C-OH}$ carbon and the isopropyl-bearing carbon. It is trisubstituted and is the most stable Zaitsev product of dehydration, keeping both methyl and isopropyl substituents on the cyclohexene ring.
